newsitem.title: USA: Spice Entertainment adopts rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Spice Entertainment adopts rights plan.

text.p: Spice Entertainment Cos Inc, which provides adult television programming, said Monday its board adopted a shareholder rights plan aimed at protecting its investors from unfair takeover tactics.

The plan provides for a dividend distribution of one right for each outstanding common share to holders of record on June 27. The plan would take effect if an acquiring party accumulates 15 percent or more of the company's common stock.

If that happens, shareholders other than the acquiring party will have the right to buy either the company's common shares or shares of the acquiring party at half the market value of those securities.
Spice Entertainment may redeem the rights at one percent for each right at any time until the tenth day after the rights become exercisable. The rights will expire on June 12, 2007.
J. Faherty, chairman and chief executive officer of the company, said details of the new rights plan will be outlined in a letter to be mailed to shareholders after the June 27 record date.
Spice Entertainment was formerly known as Graff Pay-Per-View.
